source.note: The lord of the tenth in the fifth, Mercury in a kendra, the Sun in his own sign and strong, Mars in a trikona from Mercury, and Jupiter in a trikona from the Moon or in the eleventh from Mercury, as the translation reads the last quarter. BPHS ch. 36 has the Sun in Leo with no Mars, or a second yoga of Jupiter or Mercury from the Moon and Mars in the eleventh. Read from V. Subrahmanya Sastri's 1932 translation.

source.note: A malefic in the ninth, benefics and malefics together in the fifth, and a malefic in the fourth or the eighth. The translation reads the verse's lagna-dharma as the ninth from the lagna; read as the lagna and the ninth, it would ask a malefic in the lagna too (C481). BPHS ch. 36 has benefics in the lagna and the ninth. Read from V. Subrahmanya Sastri's 1932 translation.

source.note: The ninth lord in a kendra, in its mooltrikona or at its deep exaltation, while the lagna lord is strong. The verse sets the deep exaltation on the ninth lord, as the Chowkhamba commentary and Jatakadesha's parallel read it; the translation sets it on the lagna lord (C481). BPHS ch. 36 admits the ninth lord's own and exaltation signs. Read from V. Subrahmanya Sastri's 1932 translation.

source.note: A fixed sign rising, Venus in a kendra, the Moon in the fifth and Saturn in the tenth. BPHS ch. 36 has the Moon in a trine with a benefic. Read from V. Subrahmanya Sastri's 1932 translation.

outcomes.text: a powerful sovereign of wide fame, foremost among kings of royal line, of great enjoyments, bowed to by rulers and bountiful
